map.总碱度和总硬度有什么区别，都要调吗？: What is the difference between total alkalinity and total hardness, and do both need adjusting?
map.总碱度反映水体缓冲酸碱波动的能力（以 CaCO₃ 计），总硬度反映钙镁离子总量。: Total alkalinity reflects the water's ability to buffer acid-base fluctuation (expressed as CaCO₃), while total hardness reflects the total of calcium and magnesium ions. For most water bodies, prioritize keeping alkalinity at 80~150 mg/L to stabilize pH; crustaceans such as shrimp and crab are sensitive to hardness (especially calcium and magnesium) and need hardness adjusted synchronously during molting. Baking soda raises alkalinity only, while lime and calcium chloride raise or lower hardness as well.

Long-term alkalinity >300 mg/L (as CaCO₃) together with excessive hardness may upset the ion balance, so rely on measured values and supplement as needed rather than adding heavily on a fixed schedule.
